title: Aider operating card

sections.title: Can I use this operating card as verified guidance?
paragraphs: Intermediate-level answer: No. The supplied material does not establish any verified operating procedure, command, option, version, configuration key, expected output, or recovery mechanism for Aider. Treat those details as UNKNOWN and do not rely on this card for operational guidance until its source and existing contents have been reviewed.

The current resource text was not supplied, so correct material cannot be distinguished from affected material. Reconstructing the missing text would be a rewrite, not the requested correction-only update.

sections.title: Source change and remediation
paragraphs: The cited source under review is content/resources/coding-tools/aider-operating-card.json. It is a local path with an unregistered publisher and no recorded verification. Whether the trigger was a moved source or an exceeded review cadence is UNKNOWN. The affected material is every operational claim or instruction supported only by that citation, because none can be revalidated from the supplied evidence.

Step 1: Retrieve the complete current JSON file and preserve a verbatim comparison copy. If the file cannot be retrieved, stop the update and request it from the repository owner rather than reconstructing its fields or paragraphs.

Step 2: Open the first-party HTTPS documentation and check that its final URL resolves and supports each retained operational claim. If the source does not resolve or does not support a claim, omit that claim and record it as UNKNOWN in the review notes rather than substituting an unsupported instruction.

Step 3: Compare the source-supported claims with the preserved resource and change only material affected by the stale or moved citation. If affected and unaffected text cannot be distinguished, stop and obtain the earlier source history or reviewed revision before editing.

Step 4: Confirm that the target filename is aider-operating-card.json, that id and slug match that filename, and that the identifier is unique across the shared catalogue. Then parse the completed file as JSON. If the target path, registry, or parser check is unavailable, do not publish the update and request the missing check.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence is a preserved copy of the prior resource, a successful HTTPS source-resolution record, claim-level notes showing what changed, a correction-only diff, confirmation of identifier uniqueness, and a successful JSON parse.

Verify the result by comparing the final file with the preserved copy and confirming that the diff contains only source metadata and text affected by the documented source change. Independently open every listed source, check the supporting passages, confirm the recorded verification dates, parse the file, and run the catalogue validation. If any check fails, keep the resource unpublished and return to the corresponding remediation step.
